1017:
After the preliminary plat of a proposed land subdivision has been given tentative approval by the planning commission, the subdivider may, within one year from tentative approval, submit to the planning commission:
a. A letter requesting review and approval of a final plat and giving the name and address of the person to whom the notice of the hearing by the planning commission on the final plat shall be sent.
b. Ten copies of the final plat and other related documents, as specified in this article.
1018:
The planning commission shall check the final plat for conformance with the tentatively approved preliminary plat, and with the rules and regulations of these regulations, and shall afford a hearing on the final plat, notice of the time and place of which shall be sent by the planning commission by registered or certified mail to the person designated in the letter requesting final plat review and approval, not less than five days prior to the date of hearing.
Thereafter, the planning commission shall approve or disapprove the final plat. A notation of the action shall be made on the original tracing and two prints of the final plat, including a statement of the reasons therefor if the final plat is disapproved. If action is not taken by the planning commission within 45 days of the date of the submittal, the final plat shall be considered approved and a certificate of approval shall be issued on demand. However, the applicant for approval may waive this requirement and consent to an extension of time.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1019:
Upon approval of a final plat, the subdivider shall have the final plat recorded in the office of the clerk of court of Catoosa County within 30 days or plat is void.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1021:
The final plat shall conform to and meet the specifications of the preliminary plat, with the following additions:
a. The final plat shall be clearly and legibly drawn in permanent ink on tracing cloth or other approved material. Sheet sizes shall be 17 by 21 inches, and where more than one sheet is required, an index map shall be required on the same size sheet. The final plat shall show:
1. Bearings and distances to the nearest existing street lines or benchmarks or other permanent monuments (not less than three) shall be accurately described on the plat.
2. Municipal, county and land lot lines accurately tied to the lines of the subdivision by distances and angles when such lines traverse or are reasonably close to the subdivision.
3. Exact boundary lines of the tract, determined by a field survey.
4. Name of subdivision, exact locations, widths, and names of all streets and alleys within and immediately adjoining the plat.
5. Street centerlines showing angles of deflection, angles of intersection, radii, and lengths of tangents.
6. Lot lines with dimensions to the nearest one-tenth foot and bearings to the nearest minute.
7. Lots numbered in numerical order and blocks lettered alphabetically.
8. Location, dimensions, and purposes of any easements and any areas to be reserved or dedicated for public use.
9. Accurate location, material, and description of monuments and markers.
10. Location of the sidewalk which shall be constructed a minimum of 24 inches off the back of the curb and the minimum width being 60 inches for residential and for commercial and the minimum depth of four inches. The concrete must be approved by the city prior to pouring the sidewalk.
11. A statement, either directly on the plat or in an identified attached document, of any private covenants.

1023:
Land subject to flooding, improper drainage, or erosion or that is for topographical or other reasons unsuitable for residential use shall not be platted for residential use nor for any other use that will continue or increase the danger to health, safety, or property destruction, unless the hazards can be and are corrected.
The developer shall install detention/retention structures designed by a certified engineer when there is new road construction, or in commercial or industrial developments of one acre or more.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1024: The name of the subdivision must have the approval of the planning commission. The name shall not duplicate nor closely approximate the name of an existing subdivision.
1025: Subdivisions shall be located so as to gain access over a public street.
1026:
All streets, thoroughfares, and other features of the major thoroughfare plan of the City of Ringgold shall be taken into consideration by the subdivider.
Whenever a plat proposes the dedication of land to public use that the planning commission finds not required or suitable for such public use, the planning commission shall refuse to approve the plat, and shall notify the governing body [city council] of the reasons for such action.
1027: The requirements of these regulations may be modified in the case of a large-scale community or neighborhood unit, such as a housing project or shopping center which is not subdivided into customary lots, blocks, and streets, if the development is approved by the planning commission and if it is in conformity with the purpose and intent of these regulations.
1029: Existing streets shall be continued at the same or greater width, but in no case less than the required width.
1030: Street names shall require the approval of the planning commission. Streets that are obviously in alignment with streets already existing and named shall be given the name of the existing street. Names of new streets shall not duplicate or closely approximate those of existing streets.
1031: Street jogs with centerline offsets of less than 125 feet shall not be permitted.
1032:
Except where topographic or other conditions make a greater length unavoidable, cul-de-sacs, or dead-end streets, shall not be greater in length than 500 feet. They shall be provided at the closed end with a turnaround having a property line radius of at least 50 feet with an outside pavement radius of at least 40 feet and three-foot shoulders with or without curbs and gutters. Cul-de-sacs are discouraged in all new developments.
(Mo. of 4-12-82; Ord. of 10-22-01)
1033: Where a subdivision abuts or contains a major street, a limited-access highway, or a railroad right-of-way, the planning commission may require a street approximately parallel to and on each side of such right-of-way either as a marginal-access street, or at a distance suitable for an appropriate use of the intervening land, with a nonaccess reservation. Due regard should be given requirements for approach grades and future grade separations in determining distances. Such lots shall have no access to a major street (or limited-access highway), but only to the access street.
1034: Alleys may be required at the rear of all lots used for multifamily, commercial, or industrial developments. Alleys in residential subdivisions shall not be permitted, unless the subdivider provides evidence satisfactory to the planning commission of the need for alleys.
1035: Reserving strips which control access to streets, alleys, and public grounds shall not be permitted.
1036:
Easements having a minimum width of ten feet and located along the rear lot lines shall be provided for utility lines, and underground mains and cables.
Where a subdivision is traversed by a watercourse, drainageway, channel, or stream, there shall be provided a closed stormwater or drainage system of adequate size and type as determined by the registered civil engineer. When the drainage conditions warrant, the planning commission may require a ten-foot easement between lots to be divided equally among the lots.
(a) A five-foot wide utility easement or right-of-way shall be required in addition to the easements and right-of-way of the city along all roads to be dedicated to public use in the subdivision.
(b) The five-foot easement shall run contiguous and parallel to the outer edge of easements and rights-of-way of the city along all roads to be dedicated to public use in all subdivisions heretofore constructed.
(Mo. of 4-12-82; Ord. of 10-22-01)
1037:
The developer will indicate on the final plat, in each deed, and the restrictive covenants (if any) that parking on the public right-of-way is not allowed.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1039:
The right-of-way width shall be the distance across a street from property line to property line. Minimum street right-of-way widths shall be as follows:
a. Major street widths as required by the major thoroughfare plan.
b. Collector streets, 40 feet.
c. Minor streets and dead-end street, 40 feet.
d. Alleys, 24 feet.
(Mo. of 4-12-82; Ord. of 10-22-01)
1040:
Street pavement widths shall be as follows:
a. Major street widths as required by the Georgia Highway Department, the county commissioner [commission], or the city council.
b. Collector streets, 24 feet with curb and gutters, 20 feet and three-foot shoulders without curb and gutter.
c. Minor streets and dead-end streets, 24 feet with curb and gutters, 20 feet and three-foot shoulders without curb and gutters.
(Mo. of 4-12-82; Ord. of 10-22-01)
1041:
Maximum and minimum street grades shall be as follows:
a. Major streets, not in excess of seven percent.
b. Collector streets, not in excess of ten percent.
c. Minor streets and dead-end streets and alleys, not in excess of 18 percent.
d. No street grade shall be less than one-half of one percent.
1042:
The minimum radii of centerline curvature shall be as follows:
a. Major streets, not less than 800 feet.
b. Collector streets, 200 feet.
c. Minor streets and dead-end streets and alleys, 100 feet.
1043:
Between reverse curves, there shall be [a] tangent having a length not less than the following:
a. Major streets, 200 feet.
b. Collector streets, 100 feet.
1044:
Vertical alignment shall be such that the following requirements are met:
a. Major streets shall have a sight distance of at least 500 feet at six feet above ground level.
b. Collector streets shall have a sight distance of at least 200 feet at six feet above ground level.
1045: Street intersections shall be as nearly at right angles as possible. No street intersection shall be at an angle of less than 60 degrees.
1046: The curbline radius at street intersections shall be at least 15 feet. Where the angle of street intersection is less than 90 degrees, a longer radius may be required.
1047:
In order to assure that all roads that are to be dedicated for public use and maintenance, the following procedures shall apply:
1. The preparation of all dirt subgrades shall be done according to generally accepted site grading practices. These practices include but are not limited to:
(a) No large rock, boulders, tree stumps or any other type of organic material shall be used as fill within the limits of the right-of-way.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1049:
Block lengths and widths shall be as follows:
a. Blocks shall be not greater than 1,800 feet nor less than 600 feet in length, except in unusual circumstances.
b. Blocks shall be wide enough to provide two tiers of lots of minimum depth except where abutting upon major streets, limited-access highways, or railroads or where other situations make this requirement impracticable.
1050:
Residential lots shall meet the lot width and lot area requirements of the zoning ordinance. In the absence of a zoning ordinance, residential lots shall not be less than 100 feet wide at the building line.
Residential lots shall have an area of not less than 8,500 square feet.
Commercial and industrial lots shall be adequate to provide service areas and off-street parking suitable to use intended.
Residential corner lots shall have adequate width to meet building setback requirements from both abutting streets.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1051: All lot lines shall be perpendicular or radial to street lines, unless not practicable because of topographic or other features.
1052:
A building line of not less than 25 feet from the street right-of-way shall be established on all lots.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1053: Each lot shall abut upon a dedicated public street.
1054: Double-frontage and reverse-frontage lots should be avoided except where essential to provide separation of residential development from traffic arteries or to overcome specific disadvantages of topography and orientation.
1055:
(a) There shall be a minimum of four feet of green space between the street curb and sidewalk.
(b) Prior to development, the subdivision developer shall designate at least ten percent of the total area of development (excluding streets and rights-of-way) to green space to serve as recreational property to be maintained by an association of homeowners within that subdivision. The location, size and layout of the designated area shall be submitted to the city for its review and consideration prior to development. This requirement may not be avoided by construction of the subdivision in phases.
(c) The association provided for in subsection (b) shall cause the designated green space area to be maintained suitably to provide for the needs of a majority of the subdivision's residents as determined by vote or poll of the residents. As the needs of residents may vary with time, the association shall be authorized to provide for and require that the designated area be modified or changed in accordance with any such change in needs. The association shall further be charged with enforcing restrictive covenants and prevent the creation and/or maintenance of nuisances within the subdivision.
(d) Prior to development, the subdivision developer shall submit plans for the use of streetlights within the subdivision to the city for approval. Minimum requirements for streetlights are as follows:
(1) Streetlights shall be situated no further than 200 feet apart;
(2) Streetlights must utilize bulbs of the same wattage and must be placed in such a manner to minimize glare to motorists;
(3) Streetlights may not be located on any mailbox or mailbox structure;
(4) Streetlights shall be Sternberg D650 light fixtures with 508 model fitters on black 3400 model straight fluted shafts or of comparable quality as approved by the planning commission; and
(5) Streetlights shall be maintained by an association of homeowners within the subdivision.
(e) Apartment complexes consisting of at least 100 units shall have and maintain a swimming pool and clubhouse with suitable facilities for meeting and recreation to accommodate the number of residents and/or guests likely to use the same.
(f) For any subdivision to be developed on real property adjacent to Interstate 75, there shall be a permanent buffer zone which is at least a distance 25 feet from the outer edge of the subdivision to Interstate 75. The buffer zone shall consist of at least two rows of Leyland Cypress trees (or other trees of an equivalent size and shape). Said trees shall be planted in a staggered formation and in containers of three gallons at a distance of no greater than 12 feet apart. It shall be the responsibility of the developer of the subdivision to ensure that this buffer zone is maintained in accordance with the requirements set forth herein for a period of at least two years from the completion of the subdivision. Following such time, the buffer zone shall be maintained by an association of homeowners within that subdivision.
(g) No building or structure shall be placed on or within 20 feet of any stormwater easement or stormwater drainage area owned, maintained and/or used for that such purpose by the city.
(h) Cul-de-sacs are permitted in subdivisions, provided, however, a subdivision of 100 or more lots shall have and maintain at least two points of ingress and egress.
(Ord. No. 06-0410-01, § 1, 4-10-06; Ord. No. 2013-0408-02, § 1, 4-8-13; Ord. No. 2018-0226-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
1057:
Every subdivider shall plan for and provide the following street improvements and utilities:
a. Street grading, curbs and gutters, and street base and paving, except on major or limited-access streets.
Street base and paving requirements by the city are as follows:
1. Minimum street base shall be composed of ten-inch compacted chert or six-inch compacted graded aggregate base. All base work must be acceptable to the city. Compaction may be required and all cost will be paid for by the developer.
2. Two inches of three-fourths-inch asphaltic concrete leveling binder course.
3. One inch of asphaltic concrete surface course.
b. Sanitary sewer lines and manholes storm drainage facilities where needed, and monuments and markers, all to be certified by the city's engineer whose fee will be paid for by the developer.
c. Water mains within the subdivision with connections to each lot, to be certified by the city's engineer whose fee will be paid for by the developer.
All utilities to be installed in the streets shall be placed and compacted prior to paving.
(Ord. of 10-22-01)
1059:
In lieu of the completion of the required improvements in a subdivision, the subdivider may deposit surety for the completion of such improvements as are shown on final plat submitted for final approval.
Requirements. To assure the construction and installation of required improvements the subdivider shall deliver to the Ringgold City Council a certified check, surety bond or other acceptable security in such aggregate amount as is estimated by the governing authority to be the total cost of the construction and installation of and public improvements which are the responsibility of the subdivider.
14.1. Conditions. Bonds or other surety posted shall run to the City of Ringgold and provide that the subdivider, his heirs or successors and assigns, and their agents and servants, will comply with all applicable terms, conditions, provisions, and requirements of these regulations and any other applicable requirements; will faithfully perform and complete the work of constructing and installing said facilities or improvements in accordance with these regulations and any other applicable requirements; and that the subdivider shall be responsible to the City of Ringgold for any unnecessary expense incurred through the failure of the subdivider, his heirs, successors and assigns, or their agents or servants, to complete the work of said construction in an acceptable manner, and from any damages growing out of negligence in performing or failing to perform said construction and installation. Before acceptance, any surety shall be approved by the City of Ringgold. If a bond is offered, it shall be executed by a surety or guaranty company qualified to transact business in the State of Georgia.
14.2. Duration and release. Bonds and/or other surety posted pursuant to these regulations shall be released or returned, as the case may be, at such time as the facilities guaranteed thereby have been installed and accepted. Acceptances shall be in writing accurately identifying the improvements covered. Facilities shall not be accepted unless they conform to the applicable city specifications and requirements.
14.3. Default. If the construction or installation of any improvements or facilities for which a bond or other surety is posted is not completed within three months after substantial completion of any buildings or structures which said improvements or facilities are designed to serve, or within two years after the date of recordation of the final plat, whichever is sooner, or if said construction or installation is not in accordance with applicable standards, the city may proceed to construct, install, or modify said improvements or facilities in accordance with the applicable specifications and requirements using the proceeds from such surety deposits to pay for such work. Such work may be done under contract or by city personnel. To the extent that any portion of a cash deposit is not required or used, said excess cash shall be repaid to the person making the deposit.
(a) (1) A developer or subdivider is responsible for all maintenance and upkeep to the standards in force or hereafter enacted by the city of all infrastructure including but limited to; potable water system, sanitary sewer system, stormwater collection and detention/retention system, street lights and wiring system, sidewalks, curbs, cutters, street and traffic signs, road including subbase and compacted aggregate caused to be built by him for a period of two years from the date of completion of all infrastructure.
(2) In the event a surety bond posted under this article fails for any reason to provide payment to the city where the city contends it should recover against developer or subdivider in connection with any infrastructure, the developer or subdivider shall be personally liable to the city for damages to the city and shall execute such personal guarantee on forms specified by the city.
(3) The city declares that the standards set forth for infrastructure development are mandatory and the failure to comply with said standards is a misdemeanor offense punishable in the municipal court. Each day a violation exists shall constitute a separate and continuing violation.
(4) The city declares that the violation of this Land Subdivision Ordinance is both a criminal act and a right for which civil remedies shall exist, and the city may pursue both actions simultaneously, and the pendency of the one form of action shall not be cause to abate the other.

1061: Whenever the provisions of these regulations and those of some other statute, ordinance or resolution apply to the same subject matter, that statute, ordinance or resolution requiring the highest, or more strict standard shall govern.

1063:
Purpose
The Zoning Ordinance of the City of Ringgold, Georgia regulates the use of land and buildings by dividing the City of Ringgold into districts; defining certain terms used therein; imposing regulations, prohibitions and restrictions governing the erection, construction and reconstruction of structures and buildings and the use of lands for business, industry, residence, social and other specified purposes; regulating and limiting the height of buildings and open spaces, regulating and limiting the density of population; limiting congestion on the public streets; providing for the gradual elimination of nonconforming uses of land, buildings and structures; establishing the boundaries of districts; and providing the means of enforcing said ordinance and providing a penalty for violation of said ordinance, and repeal conflicting ordinances.
(Ord. No. 2014-0224, § 1, 2-24-14)

1066:
The mayor and council of the City of Ringgold enact this ordinance under the exercise of powers conferred upon it by the Georgia State Constitution, Article IX, Section II, Paragraph IV (Zoning Procedures Law).
The purpose of said zoning ordinance is to lessen congestion in the streets; to secure safety from fire, panic and other dangers; to promote health and the general welfare; to provide adequate light and air; to prevent the overcrowding of land; to protect property values; to avoid undue concentration of population; to facilitate the adequate provisions of transportation, water, sewerage, schools, parks and other public requirements; to conserve the value of buildings and encourage the most appropriate use of land throughout the corporate area, all in accordance with a comprehensive zoning ordinance for the City of Ringgold.
